1.title: The Marol Depot Road Payroll Robbery
1.summary: A payroll van carrying the weekly wages of a logistics firm was waylaid on Marol Depot Road. The security escort was struck down and the cash bag taken. The cashier is unhurt and the guard is in hospital. The company wants it treated as a simple highway robbery.
1.resumePoint: Supplementary Investigation — All files intact under BNSS §193(9)

fir.narrative: The complainant Nitin Bhosale, manager of Shree Siddhivinayak Logistics, reports that on the day before yesterday between about 14:05 and 14:20 hours, an unknown person or persons caused the payroll van of the firm to stop on Marol Depot Road just before the culvert, and dishonestly took from the van a pay bag containing Rs 4,18,000 in cash meant for the wages of the depot staff. The van had been forced to halt, the driver was threatened, and the bag was snatched away. The firm delayed one day in reporting because it first attempted to trace the money internally through its accountant. On enquiry it is revealed that the movement of the payroll van and the cash was known only to a small number of persons connected with the firm, which suggests the involvement of an insider. The complainant therefore prays that an FIR be registered and the matter investigated.

exhibits.name: Iron crowbar, black painted
exhibits.described: A 62 cm iron crowbar, black paint worn at the claw. Paint transfer and a partial palm impression on the shaft.
exhibits.significance: The tool used to force the van's rear shutter. Fingerprint and trace analysis link it to a person and to the van.

custody.note: Recovered on the disclosure of (accused) in the presence of Suresh Kadam, shopkeeper and Anita Fernandes, resident.

exhibits.why: Admissible. Lab support at 45% confidence.

exhibits.name: Torn currency strap and paper wrapper
exhibits.described: A torn paper currency strap printed with a bank name and a rubber-stamp date, plus a wrapper fragment.
exhibits.significance: Connects the scene to the specific bundle withdrawn by the firm from its bank that morning.

custody.note: Seized and deposited in the malkhana register.
Forensic examination completed and exhibit returned.

exhibits.why: Admissible. Lab support at 45% confidence.

exhibits.described: A white cotton kerchief, bloodstained, caught in the road-shoulder gravel. Visible only under oblique lighting.
exhibits.significance: The guard is O positive. If this blood is a different group, it belongs to an assailant who was injured — a direct link to a person.

custody.note: Seized and deposited in the malkhana register.
Forensic examination completed and exhibit returned.

exhibits.why: Admissible. Lab support at 45% confidence.

exhibits.significance: Partial plate of the blue pickup and the number of occupants. Admissible only with a hashed copy and a dual-signed s.63 certificate.

custody.note: Seized and deposited in the malkhana register.

custody.note: Seized and deposited in the malkhana register.

persons.canvassQuote: I was preparing tea when I heard tyres screeching loudly and shouting near the cash van. A white getaway vehicle raced past immediately after.
persons.observation: I was boiling morning milk when I heard tyres screeching. Two masked men struck the guard and grabbed the green currency bag. One dropped an iron rod near the rear wheel.
persons.respectableStatement: I have run Anand Tea Stall for 22 years. Local police and all shopkeepers know me as an honest, respectable resident without any criminal history or bias.
persons.consentResponse: Yes, Inspector Sahab. I am ready to stand as an independent panch witness and sign the seizure memo under BNSS §103 according to law.

persons.name: Rukhsana Fernandes
persons.canvassQuote: I saw suspicious movement behind the transformer shed. Someone dropped an object near the drain.
persons.observation: I saw a man hastily toss a heavy metallic object into the weeds behind the drainage culvert before leaping into the getaway car.
persons.respectableStatement: I operate a registered grocery shop and have resided here for 18 years. Completely impartial and neutral.
persons.consentResponse: If the police ensure I won't face repeated court adjournments during shop hours, I am prepared to sign the seizure memo.

persons.name: Baban Kadam
persons.canvassQuote: I heard shouting while fixing a meter box. Did not step out because these things get dangerous.
persons.observation: I heard loud shouting from the road. I peeked through the window and saw two men running with a duffel bag, then quickly bolted my door.
persons.respectableStatement: I am a peaceful resident of Room 12 living with my family.
persons.consentResponse: Sahab, I have small grandchildren. I am terrified of criminal retaliation. I will tell you what I saw, but please do not make me sign panchnamas in court.

persons.name: Shailesh Gupta
persons.canvassQuote: I was setting up my kiosk at 8:30 AM. Observed two individuals loitering near the bus shelter for half an hour.
persons.observation: Two men in caps were pacing back and forth looking at their wristwatches and watching the bank road before the van pulled up.
persons.respectableStatement: I have operated this kiosk for 8 years. Neutral independent vendor with valid municipal trade license.
persons.consentResponse: Yes, Sir. I will witness the seizure and put my signature on the memo.

persons.name: Mahesh Shinde
persons.canvassQuote: A white sedan came in early morning asking for immediate puncture repair; driver seemed extremely agitated.
persons.observation: A white sedan with scuffed wheel rims pulled in at 7:50 AM asking to check tire pressure in a hurry. The driver had mud on his trousers and was constantly watching the main junction.
persons.respectableStatement: I am a registered automotive mechanic with a licensed commercial workshop. Independent and impartial inhabitant.
persons.consentResponse: I am an independent tradesman. I will act as a respectable panch witness under BNSS §103.

persons.name: Kishore Jadhav
persons.canvassQuote: Someone purchased a heavy 340mm hexagonal iron rod from my shop two days prior to the incident.
persons.observation: A stocky man matching suspect Imran Pawar bought a reinforced hexagonal iron crowbar and paid in cash without taking a receipt.
persons.respectableStatement: I have owned Jadhav Hardware for 30 years. Impartial business owner in this market.
persons.consentResponse: If you record my statement properly and minimize court delays, I will sign the panchnama.

persons.name: Latika Gaikwad
persons.canvassQuote: Saw two men abandon a motorbike in the back lane and quickly walk through the market corridor towards the bus stop.
persons.observation: They were wearing dark windcheaters despite the morning heat and walking briskly with heavy gym bags towards the market exit.
persons.respectableStatement: I run my boutique peacefully. No connections or bias regarding any party.
persons.consentResponse: Yes Officer, citizens must help the police maintain community safety. I will sign as a panch witness.

persons.name: Ganesh Tandel
persons.canvassQuote: I was checking the drainage sluice valve when I spotted tire skid marks leading towards the overgrown culvert bank.
persons.observation: Found fresh tire tread impressions in the wet mud along the culvert path and a discarded cloth with dark stains near Grid F4.
persons.respectableStatement: I am a permanent municipal pump operator with the Municipal Corporation. Neutral, respectable public servant.
persons.consentResponse: Being a public servant, I understand my civic duty. I will gladly sign the seizure panchnama under BNSS §103.

persons.name: Rafiq Ansari

persons.respectableStatement: I run a licensed scrap yard here.
persons.consentResponse: Babu, I beg you, do not make me a court witness! The local goons will burn down my scrap yard. I cannot sign court papers!

persons.name: Santosh Salvi

2.title: Theft from a locked shop — Shivaji Market
2.summary: Reported occurrence at Shivaji Market. Theft from a locked shop. Thorough investigation required; the schedule was known in advance, which suggests inside involvement.

fir.narrative: Nitin Bhonsle, Account Cashier, Sunrise Logistics Pvt Ltd withdrew cash ₹418000, mostly in ₹500 denominations, on Monday Morning. While transporting the cash to Sector 9, he, alongwith Mr. Ramzan, was stopped by two armed unknown men around Marol Depot Road. Mr. Ramzan was hit by the gun on head which caused head injury and visible external bleeding. The victims claim it to be a planned robbery by unknown persons.

trial.judgment:
IN THE COURT OF THE SESSIONS JUDGE, PUNE
Special Trial Case № 2417/682 / 2026
State of Maharashtra (through Crime Branch) versus Accused

JUDGMENT:
1. The prosecution has submitted a formal charge sheet under Section 193 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) charging the accused with offences punishable under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS).

2. The court has minutely evaluated the depositions recorded under BNSS s.180/183, the panchnamas, and the admissible material placed on record. The aggregate weight of admissible proof stands at 410.

3. Evidence Evaluation & Legal Assessment:
   - Exhibits tendered and admitted: Recovered tool / instrument of offence (Weight: 45), Biological trace on fabric (Weight: 50), Surveillance footage (Weight: 65), Telecom call detail records (Weight: 65), Financial records / money trail (Weight: 45), Impression or trace from the scene (Weight: 40), Concealed lock-cutter & grey duffel bag (Weight: 25), RBI ₹500 Currency Note (№ 7AB 849201) (Weight: 45).
   - Discovery disclosures under Section 23 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 were duly corroborated by recovery memos executed in the presence of independent respectable witnesses.

4. Finding of the Court:
   Accused held guilty beyond reasonable doubt. Complete chain of circumstantial and direct evidence established.

5. Order:
   Sentenced to 5 years Rigorous Imprisonment under BNS ss. 309, 115, 61 with a fine of ₹25,000.

stages.name: Cognizance & framing of charges
stages.procedure: The court takes cognizance of the charge sheet, satisfies itself there is ground to proceed, and frames the charges the accused must answer.
stages.note: A defective or delayed charge sheet is examined here first. Charges may be altered or dropped at this stage.

stages.name: Prosecution evidence (examination-in-chief)
stages.procedure: The prosecution examines its witnesses in chief and marks its exhibits. Each electronic record must carry its s.63 certificate as it is tendered.
stages.note: This is where an uncertified or tainted exhibit is exposed, because it cannot lawfully be marked.

stages.name: Cross-examination by the defence
stages.procedure: Defence counsel tests every witness: omissions, contradictions, improvements and the chain of custody of every exhibit.
stages.note: A hostile or inconsistent witness is broken here. Custody breaks are fatal at this stage.

stages.name: Defence evidence
stages.procedure: The accused may lead evidence, including a plea of alibi or a claim of a verifiable alibi contradicted by the prosecution record.
stages.note: An unverified alibi on the file becomes a live doubt here.

stages.name: Examination of the accused
stages.procedure: The court puts the incriminating circumstances to each accused personally, and records their answers.
stages.note: Material not put to the accused cannot be used to convict them.

stages.name: Final arguments
stages.procedure: Prosecution and defence address the court on the evidence, the presumptions, and the applicable sections.
stages.note: Counsel's written summary of arguments forms part of this.

stages.name: Judgment
stages.procedure: The court delivers a reasoned judgment, either convicting or acquitting, and states the points for determination with its findings.
stages.note: Every accused is entitled to the benefit of reasonable doubt.

snapshot.title: Theft from a locked shop — Shivaji Market
snapshot.summary: Reported occurrence at Shivaji Market. Theft from a locked shop. Thorough investigation required; the schedule was known in advance, which suggests inside involvement.

fir.narrative: Nitin Bhonsle, Account Cashier, Sunrise Logistics Pvt Ltd withdrew cash ₹418000, mostly in ₹500 denominations, on Monday Morning. While transporting the cash to Sector 9, he, alongwith Mr. Ramzan, was stopped by two armed unknown men around Marol Depot Road. Mr. Ramzan was hit by the gun on head which caused head injury and visible external bleeding. The victims claim it to be a planned robbery by unknown persons.

Mr. Ramzan was hit by the gun on head which caused head injury and visible external bleeding. The victims claim it to be a planned robbery by unknown persons.

fir.narrative: Nitin Bhonsle, Account Cashier, Sunrise Logistics Pvt Ltd withdrew cash ₹418000, mostly in ₹500 denominations, on Monday Morning. While transporting the cash to Sector 9, he, alongwith Mr. Ramzan, was stopped by two armed unknown men around Marol Depot Road. Mr. Ramzan was hit by the gun on head which caused head injury and visible external bleeding. The victims claim it to be a planned robbery by unknown persons.

Mr. Ramzan was hit by the gun on head which caused head injury and visible external bleeding. The victims claim it to be a planned robbery by unknown persons.

fir.narrative: Nitin Bhonsle, Account Cashier, Sunrise Logistics Pvt Ltd withdrew cash ₹418000, mostly in ₹500 denominations, on Monday Morning. While transporting the cash to Sector 9, he, alongwith Mr. Ramzan, was stopped by two armed unknown men around Marol Depot Road. Mr. Ramzan was hit by the gun on head which caused head injury and visible external bleeding. The victims claim it to be a planned robbery by unknown persons.
